additional_requirements: depressive_episode is present for the majority of the total duration of the active and residual portions of the illness (Criterion C)
delusions_and_hallucinations occur for 2 or more weeks in the absence of a major mood episode (Criterion B)

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S021.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
S021.description: Symptoms where speech or thought appears scattered and difficult to follow due to a lack of logical or consistent flow.

subtypes.Derailment or Loose Associations: A speech pattern of switching rapidly from one topic to another with no logical connection between thoughts.
subtypes.Tangentiality: Speech that deviates entirely from the question and fails to answer directly.
subtypes.Incoherence or Word Salad: Severe fragmentation of speech and sentence structure, making it nearly impossible to understand.
subtypes.Neologisms: Using made-up words that have meaning only to the individual.
subtypes.Clang Associations: Speech governed by sounds, such as rhyming, rather than the meaning of words.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.

subtypes.Childlike Silliness: Inappropriate, childish, or illogical behavior appearing in situations.
subtypes.Stupor: No psychomotor activity; not actively relating to environment.
subtypes.Catalepsy: Passive induction of a posture held against gravity.
subtypes.Waxy Flexibility: Slight, even resistance to positioning by examiner.
subtypes.Mutism: No, or very little, verbal response despite the ability to speak.
subtypes.Negativism: Opposition or no response to instructions or external stimuli without apparent motive.
subtypes.Posturing: Spontaneous and active maintenance of a posture against gravity.
subtypes.Mannerism: Odd, circumstantial caricature of normal actions.
subtypes.Agitation: Excessive motor activity without obvious external cause.
subtypes.Grimacing: Contorted facial expressions irrelevant to the situation.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

info.persona: Charles Sweeting is a methodical, community‑driven handyman who balances competitive ambition with a warm, gregarious spirit, all while never missing a Sunday gospel rehearsal or a chance to perfect his secret mango‑chili fish fry.
info.professional_persona: Charles Sweeting, a seasoned handyperson and community organizer, blends his decades of construction trades expertise with meticulous budgeting and event planning to run senior‑center DIY workshops and a part‑time handyman service for older neighbors, leveraging his methodical, competitive drive and sociable nature.
info.cultural_background: Charles is an African‑American who grew up in the South before moving to South Florida in his twenties. His cultural identity is shaped by the traditions of the Black church, the music of gospel, blues, and jazz, and the communal celebrations of Juneteenth and Caribbean festivals common in Broward County. He maintains strong ties to his extended family and the local Black community, valuing oral storytelling, shared meals, and mutual support. His experiences as a widower have deepened his involvement in senior networks and volunteer groups, where he both contributes to and draws strength from the rich cultural fabric of Fort Lauderdale's African‑American population.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Charles enjoys a mix of social and solitary pursuits that reflect his outgoing nature and curiosity. He frequents the marina for fishing trips and occasional boat outings, participates in the weekly bridge club at the community center, and volunteers in the church choir and gospel outreach programs. He loves cooking soul‑food classics with occasional Caribbean twists, tending his vegetable garden, and walking the beachfront parks. He also takes part in local Juneteenth parades and senior fitness classes, staying active both physically and socially.
info.sports_persona: Charles Sweeting follows the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Miami Marlins, rows with the local senior rowing club at the marina, and keeps fit through brisk walks in the beachfront park and weekly low‑impact aerobics classes.
info.arts_persona: Charles Sweeting immerses himself in gospel music, singing with his church choir while collecting vinyls of Aretha Franklin, Marvin Gaye, and contemporary soul artist Leon Bridges, and enjoys occasional theater outings to see productions of August Wilson's plays at the local community theater.
info.travel_persona: Charles Sweeting plans his trips with a blend of careful budgeting and spontaneous curiosity, favoring weekend road trips along the Atlantic Coast to historic Charleston and Savannah, a yearly cruise to the Bahamas to sample fresh catch, and dreaming of a cultural pilgrimage to New Orleans' French Quarter to explore its culinary and musical heritage.
info.culinary_persona: Charles Sweeting, an adept home chef, perfects soul‑food staples like fried catfish, collard greens simmered with smoked turkey, and sweet potato pie, while adding Caribbean twists such as mango‑chili glaze and coconut‑milk‑based sauces, often sourcing fresh shrimp from the marina and using okra, hot pepper, and scallions to craft bold flavors.

info.persona: Amber Blackburn is a curious, organized retiree who blends solitary artistic pursuits with community mentorship, savoring quiet mornings, vibrant watercolors, and the occasional indulgence in garden‑fresh meals, and they cherish each slow, deliberate brushstroke as a meditation.
info.professional_persona: Amber Blackburn, a retired clerical assistant from a regional hospital, leverages decades of scheduling, budgeting, and record‑keeping expertise to orchestrate community art workshops and senior craft classes, blending meticulous organization with a quiet curiosity for heritage and aesthetics, and they enjoy sharing this knowledge with younger volunteers.
info.cultural_background: Amber was born in the early 1950s in a small Midwestern town and raised in a middle-class, Protestant family that emphasized hard work, modesty, and community service. Relocating to the Houston-area in the 1970s, she embraced the blend of Southern hospitality and the multicultural vibrancy of Fort Bend County. Her cultural identity is rooted in traditional American folk customs—church choir singing, family potlucks, and seasonal gardening—while also appreciating the diverse artistic expressions found in Texas, such as regional crafts and Southwestern art. These influences shape her respect for heritage, her dedication to volunteerism, and her preference for intimate, supportive social circles.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Amber enjoys solitary pursuits that satisfy her curiosity and love of beauty. She regularly reads historical fiction and biographies, immerses herself in watercolor painting of Texas landscapes, and tends a modest garden of native wildflowers and herbs. Birdwatching at dawn provides quiet reflection, while knitting and quilting allow her to create handcrafted gifts for close friends and family. In small-group settings, she participates in a weekly book club of six members, attends intimate art exhibitions at neighborhood galleries, and volunteers to lead craft workshops for seniors at the local community center. Genealogy research and visits to the county archives also occupy her leisure time, connecting her personal history with the broader story of Fort Bend County.
info.sports_persona: Amber Blackburn enjoys gentle early‑morning birdwatching walks in her backyard, participates in a low‑impact tai chi class at the senior center, follows the Houston Astros with fervor, and supports the Houston Rockets by watching games at a local café, embodying a relaxed yet socially connected approach to fitness, and they treasure the quiet camaraderie of these activities.
info.arts_persona: Amber Blackburn’s artistic life revolves around watercolor landscapes of Texas Hill Country, regular visits to the Houston Museum of Fine Arts to view works by Claude Monet and Georgia O’Keeffe, and leading quilting circles that celebrate the fiber artistry of Texan folk painters like Penelope Tuffnell, intertwining personal creation with deep appreciation for both classic and regional masters, and they often reference these influences in their own craft workshops.
info.travel_persona: Amber Blackburn prefers carefully planned short‑haul trips, such as weekend pilgrimages to the historic county archives in La Grange, a yearly drive to Galveston’s seaside art fairs, and occasional overseas genealogical research tours to the British Isles, balancing curiosity with the comfort of familiar hotel chains and a modest travel budget, and they cherish each quiet sunrise over a new landscape as a source of fresh inspiration.
info.culinary_persona: Amber Blackburn delights in cooking with fresh herbs from her garden, often preparing roasted chicken seasoned with rosemary and thyme, a side of wildflower‑infused honey‑glazed carrots, and baking pecan pie scented with a pinch of cinnamon, while still enjoying classic Texas‑style brisket at family gatherings, and they savor the ritual of stitching together flavors as an extension of their quilting practice.

info.persona: Nestor Olivo is a curious, art‑infused psychiatric aide who channels youthful energy into sketching murals, juggling a tight budget with occasional splurges, and they balance compassion with a penchant for late‑night coffee and missed sleep.
info.professional_persona: Nestor Olivo, a 22‑year‑old psychiatric patient support aide, blends clinical vigilance with compassionate communication, leveraging bilingual fluency and a flair for art‑based activities to enrich patient engagement while they maintain organized yet adaptable care routines.
info.cultural_background: Nestor is a second‑generation Mexican‑American whose parents emigrated from Michoacán. He grew up bilingual, speaking Spanish at home and English at school, and celebrates traditions such as Día de los Muertos and family gatherings centered around homemade tamales and pozole. The vibrant colors and storytelling of Mexican folk art influenced his own artistic pursuits. Living in Upper Marlboro, he balances his heritage with the multicultural fabric of Prince George’s County, participating in local Mexican community events while also engaging with the broader American cultural scene.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In his free time, Nestor channels his curiosity and love for art into sketching street scenes and experimenting with mixed‑media murals. He frequents local galleries and indie film screenings to stay inspired. Music, especially indie rock and traditional Latin rhythms, fuels his creativity. He enjoys cooking family recipes—tamales, mole, and fresh salsas—while sharing meals with friends. Outside the arts, he plays pick‑up soccer, hikes the Patuxent Trail, reads psychology and self‑development books, and volunteers with neighborhood mural projects that involve at‑risk teens.
info.sports_persona: Nestor Olivo joins pick‑up soccer games at the local rec center, hikes the Patuxent Trail on weekends, and roots for D.C. United and the Washington Capitals, maintaining a casual fitness routine that they balance between teamwork and solo outdoor runs.
info.arts_persona: Nestor Olivo spends evenings sketching street scenes, curates mixed‑media murals inspired by artists like JR and Banksy, and draws creative fuel from indie rock bands such as The Strokes and traditional rhythmic beats by Los Lobos, while they regularly attend gallery openings and indie film screenings.
info.travel_persona: Nestor Olivo prefers spontaneous road trips to nearby historic towns like Alexandria and Shenandoah National Park, and they also dream of backpacking through the streets of Barcelona and exploring the vibrant markets of Oaxaca, balancing limited student finances with a love for culturally rich experiences.
info.culinary_persona: Nestor Olivo enjoys cooking family recipes such as tamales, mole, and fresh salsa, experimenting with ingredients like masa, dried chilies, chocolate, and cilantro, while they hover at an enthusiastic home‑chef level, often inviting friends over for communal meals.
